'''Leonard Ross Fisher''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|OAM}} (born 1942) is an [[Australians|Australian]] [[physicist]], and visiting senior research fellow at the [[University of Bristol]], [[UK]]. He is known for his research into everyday topics, such as the optimal way to [[Dunking (biscuit)|dunk]] a biscuit, and the optimum use of cheese in a [[cheese sandwich]].

== Education ==
Fisher received a BSc in chemistry and pure mathematics,<ref>{{cite web|title=Dr Len Fisher: About Me|url=https://www.lenfisherscience.com/about-me/|access-date=19 March 2021}}</ref>{{Better source needed|date=March 2021}} and an MSc in radiation chemistry from the [[University of Sydney]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Fisher|first=Leonard Ross|url=https://sydney.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/permalink/61USYD_INST/1c0ug48/alma991027147389705106|title=The dosimetry of a 61pm 147β-radiation source|publisher=[[University of Sydney]]|year=1965|type=M.Sc. Thesis|oclc=221182218}}</ref> He has a PhD in physics of surfaces from the [[University of New South Wales]].<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Fisher|first=Leonard Ross|title=Properties of curved liquid/vapour interfaces|publisher=[[University of New South Wales]]|year=1980|doi=10.26190/unsworks/7315 |type=Ph.D Thesis|hdl=1959.4/61664|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

== Career ==
Fisher has been a visiting senior research fellow in the school of physics at the University of Bristol since 1992.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.abc.net.au/radionational/programs/scienceshow/len-fisher/10771308 |title=The Science Show |date=1 February 2019 |access-date=19 March 2021 |work=[[Radio Australia]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=
https://orcid.org/0000-0003-2880-1152 |title=Len Fisher |access-date=19 March 2021 |work=[[ORCID]]}}</ref>

=== Research ===
In 1998, Fisher published a study on the optimal way to dunk a biscuit. The study concluded that 10 times more flavour is released from a biscuit if it has first been dunked in a hot drink. This research was funded by [[McVities]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/220400.stm |title=No more flunking on dunking |date=25 November 1998 |access-date=19 March 2021 |work=[[BBC News]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fisher |first1=L.|title=Physics takes the biscuit|journal=Nature|volume=397|pages=469|year=1999|doi=10.1038/17203|bibcode=1999Natur.397..469F |issue=6719|s2cid=4404966|doi-access=free}}</ref>

In 2000, Fisher studied the absorption of [[gravy]] by a [[roast dinner]]. He found that 700,000 litres of gravy is wasted every week in the UK when it is poured on food and not consumed.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/1047698.stm |title=Gallons of gravy wasted |date=30 November 2000 |access-date=19 March 2021 |work=[[BBC News]]}}</ref> He also calculated a gravy absorption index, and published a set of rules to maximise the absorption of gravy by food.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2000/nov/30/uknews |title=Physics bids to halt gravy drain |date=30 November 2000 |access-date=19 March 2021 |work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> Following on from this work, in 2001, he researched the best bread to absorb gravy with, concluding that [[ciabatta]] soaks up the most.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/1730817.stm |title=Gravy boffin uses his loaf |date=27 December 2001 |access-date=19 March 2021 |work=[[BBC News]]}}</ref>

In 2003, Fisher produced a report for the British Cheese Board, titled "Optimum Use of Cheese in a Cheese Sandwich".<ref>{{cite report |author=Len Fisher |date=24 September 2003 |access-date=19 March 2021 |title=Optimum Use of Cheese in a Cheese Sandwich |url=https://www.lenfisherscience.com/the-optimum-cheese-sandwich/ |publisher=British Cheese Board}}</ref> He found that the optimum thickness for the filling in a cheese sandwich is dependent on the type of cheese used, and that the sandwich should be made with a light spread of butter or margarine to enhance the flavour of the cheese.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/bristol/somerset/3171068.stm |title=Scientists 'perfect' cheese sandwich |date=7 October 2003 |access-date=19 March 2021 |work=[[BBC News]]}}</ref> This research has drawn criticism for being 'frivolous'.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/magazine/8270688.stm |title=Is there any point to 'frivolous' academic research? |date=24 September 2009 |access-date=19 March 2021 |author=Denise Winterman |work=[[BBC News]]}}</ref>

== Publications ==
* ''How to Dunk a Doughnut: The Science of Everyday Life'' (2002) 
* ''Weighing the Soul: The Evolution of Scientific Ideas'' (2004)
* ''Rock, Paper, Scissors: Game Theory in Everyday Life'' (2008)<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/is-israel-becoming-a-mafia-state/ |title=Is Israel becoming a mafia state? |author=[[Simona Weinglass]] |date=11 September 2017 |newspaper=[[The Times of Israel]] |access-date=19 March 2021}}</ref>
* ''The Perfect Swarm: The Science of Complexity in Everyday Life'' (2009)<ref>{{cite news |url=https://archive.boston.com/ae/books/articles/2009/11/29/why_we_do_the_things_we_do/ |title=Why we do the things we do |author=George Scialabba |date=29 November 2009 |newspaper=[[Boston Globe]] |access-date=19 March 2021}}</ref>
* ''Crashes, Crises and Calamities: How We Can Use Science to Read the Early-Warning Signs'' (2011)

== Awards ==
Fisher was presented with the [[Ig Nobel Prize]] for Physics, in 1999, for calculating the optimal way to dunk a biscuit.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sci/tech/462987.stm |title=Brits take the biscuit |date=4 October 1999 |access-date=19 March 2021 |work=[[BBC News]]}}</ref>

In 2004, Fisher was named Science Writer of the Year by the [[American Institute of Physics]] for ''How to Dunk a Doughnut: The Science of Everyday Life''.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bluemountainsgazette.com.au/story/5860370/making-science-part-of-us/ |title=Communicating science: Dr Len Fisher's grand plan |author=Jennie Curtin |date=26 January 2019 |newspaper=Blue Mountain Gazette |access-date=19 March 2021}}</ref>

In 2019, Fisher was awarded the [[Order of Australia#Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM)|Medal of the Order of Australia]] for his contribution to science.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr Leonard Ross Fisher|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/2003394|access-date=21 March 2021|website=It's An Honour}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.wiltshiretimes.co.uk/news/17437973.scientist-given-australia-medal/ |title=Scientist given Australia medal |author=John Baker |date=16 February 2019 |newspaper=[[Wiltshire Times]] |access-date=19 March 2021}}</ref>
